sentences.text: The Korean War was triggered when North Korean forces invaded South Korea on June 25, 1950.
During the June 25, 1950, invasion of South Korea, North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel.
The North Korean People's Army, or NKPA, carried out the invasion of South Korea on June 25, 1950.
The North Korean invasion began when troops crossed the 38th parallel and entered South Korea.
The North Korean attack on June 25, 1950, was a surprise invasion that quickly captured Seoul, South Korea's capital.
The United States intervened in the Korean War to prevent communism from spreading, consistent with the Cold War strategy of containment.
The Korean War was the Cold War's first major military conflict and served as an important test of the containment doctrine.
As the first test of the Cold War doctrine of containment, the Korean War demonstrated the United States' commitment to halting communist expansion without provoking a global conflict.

General Douglas MacArthur proposed expanding the war into China and using nuclear weapons, spurring internal debate over containing communism versus risking global conflict and ultimately keeping the war confined to the Korean Peninsula.
The United States believed South Korea's fall would embolden communist leaders to threaten other countries closer to the West, reinforcing its rationale for intervention.
The United States intervened in the Korean War to prevent the spread of communism, in accordance with the Cold War policy of containment.
North Korea's invasion of South Korea on June 25, 1950, directly triggered the involvement of the United States military.
Following the North Korean invasion, the United States committed troops to defend South Korea, while President Truman authorized General Douglas MacArthur to provide air and naval support.
After the North Korean invasion, the United States led a United Nations coalition to defend South Korea, with United Nations Security Council Resolution 83 authorizing military assistance.
The Korean War produced a significant increase in military spending, contributing to the development of a powerful military-industrial complex in the United States.
President Truman's dismissal of General Douglas MacArthur triggered a political firestorm and seriously damaged Truman's approval ratings, contributing to the end of his presidency.
President Truman's firing of General Douglas MacArthur for insubordination was highly unpopular and shocked the American political system.

The Korean War intensified public fears of communist subversion, prompting investigations by the House Un-American Activities Committee and fostering belief in widespread communist infiltration of American institutions.
The Korean War concluded with the signing of an armistice on July 27, 1953.
The armistice that ended the Korean War was a truce rather than a peace treaty, so the conflict remains technically ongoing.
Because no formal peace treaty was ever signed to end the Korean War, the conflict remains officially unresolved and technically ongoing.
Fighting in the Korean War ended in a stalemate, without a clear winner or loser.
The armistice restored the boundary along the 38th parallel and established the Demilitarized Zone, a fortified buffer set at 2.5 miles wide.
The Korean War began on June 25, 1950, when North Korea crossed the 38th parallel and invaded South Korea, seeking to reunite the peninsula under communist rule by force.
The Korean War ended with an armistice signed on July 27, 1953, rather than a formal peace treaty, leaving North and South Korea technically at war.
The Korean Peninsula remains divided along the 38th parallel, a boundary between North and South Korea that has been maintained since the war.
The Korean War led to the creation of a demilitarized zone along the 38th parallel that remains heavily fortified and actively monitored.

The Korean War caused massive civilian and military casualties, with estimates indicating more than two million Korean deaths and the loss of up to 20 percent of the population through war or starvation.
On June 25, 1950, the United Nations Security Council passed Resolution 82, authorizing member states to provide military assistance to South Korea in response to North Korea's invasion.
The United States led a United Nations coalition during the Korean War, and American forces supplied most of the coalition's combat power.
The Korean War ended with an armistice signed on July 27, 1953, by North Korea, South Korea, China, and the United Nations, but no formal peace treaty was ever ratified.
The United States defense strategy of January 1950 excluded Korea from its defensive perimeter, leaving the peninsula vulnerable to attack.
General MacArthur believed China would not enter the war and pushed United Nations forces beyond the 38th parallel, provoking Chinese intervention.
China entered the Korean War to support North Korea against United Nations forces that were led by the United States.
China feared that United Nations advances, particularly toward the Yalu River, would cause encirclement or regime change in North Korea, prompting Chinese intervention.
Through neutral diplomats, China warned the United States that it would intervene to protect its national security if American forces advanced too close to the Chinese border.
Mao Zedong argued that allowing the United States to occupy all of Korea would weaken communist revolutionary power in Asia and permit American influence to spread negatively throughout the Far East.
China's initial objective in the Korean War was not to conquer South Korea but to preserve North Korea as a buffer state.
President Truman rejected General MacArthur's proposals to expand the Korean War into China and use nuclear weapons against communist forces.
General MacArthur advocated pushing North Korean forces beyond the 38th parallel and expanding the war into China, including through the use of nuclear weapons.
President Truman opposed using nuclear weapons in Korea because he viewed such action as a risk that could lead to a world war.
President Eisenhower pledged to end the Korean War in an early and honorable manner and personally visited the Korean front to evaluate the situation.
